div.div:
as-sūdasso (ads- ), ĕre,
I.v. intens. n. [from sudo, as capesso from capio, lacesso from lacio], to fall into a violent sweat, to sweat profusely: “corculum adsudassit jam ex metu,” Plaut. Cas. 2, 6, 9 dub. (perh. assudescit).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
